About this manual#

HDX Inspect is a Flutter application for inspecting machinery and equipment in the field, capturing sign-off from the inspector and the customer, and producing a branded PDF certificate for each machine. It runs on Windows, Android and iOS. Each device works fully offline against its own encrypted local database and synchronises through a shared Google Drive store.

This manual is task-oriented. It walks through everything an inspector or office administrator does day to day — from signing in, through a complete inspection, to distributing and correcting certificates, managing the schedule, and configuring the app. It reflects HDX Inspect v4.3.0.

Who should read it#

  • Inspectors — perform checks in the field, capture photos and readings, and obtain signatures. See Getting started, Performing an inspection, and Reports.
  • Administrators / office staff — additionally manage customers, machines, templates, accounts, the Drive store, scheduling and exports. Admin-only features are marked (Admin) throughout.

How to read the call-out boxes#

Three kinds of highlighted box appear in this manual:

Tip

A practical suggestion that makes a task easier or avoids a common mistake.

Important — read this

A point you must not miss — usually about losing access, losing work, or a destructive action.

Honest limitation

An honest statement of what the app does not guarantee. HDX Inspect has no central server, so some protections you might assume are present are deliberately not claimed. These boxes tell you where.

What's new in v4.3.0 (November 2026)#

  • Delivery notes are created automatically. The work hours, travel time and distance you record on an inspection become lines on the visit's delivery note as soon as the inspection is finalised — one note per customer and day, left as a draft for you to review, finalise and have signed. See chapter 11.
  • The Charging tab is gone. Its CSV export now sits on the Billing tab's delivery-notes list (§11.3); invoices are built by combining delivery notes (§12.2). The separate Charging permission no longer exists.
  • Easier navigation on phones. The bottom bar now holds every destination and scrolls sideways, and you can swipe across the screen to move between destinations. The More button is gone. With a larger phone font size the destination names no longer wrap onto two lines (§2.5).
  • An introduction, hints and this manual in the app. A short introduction on first sign-in, a one-time hint on each main screen, a ? button that opens this manual at the right chapter, and a User manual link next to the privacy policy (§2.7).
  • Company profile branding. Large logos are scaled down automatically instead of being refused, the logo has three print sizes, a letterhead banner image can be added, and the slogan, footer lines and banner can be aligned left, centred or right (§13.3).
  • Checklist templates can be archived and restored (§10.3), and a signed delivery note now shows the recipient's signature reliably (§12.5).
  • Sync recovers by itself after a dropped connection, and Settings has a Re-check Drive store action (§13.4, chapter 14).

Release note — update all devices together

Update every device before you edit a company profile on this version. v4.3.0 adds the logo size, banner image and alignment settings to the shared dataset (dataset format 10). A device still on v4.2.0 or older cannot read a format-10 dataset: it stops syncing and says that this app version is too old for the shared data store and must be updated on this device. Nothing is lost — local work on that device continues and syncs again once it is updated — but until every device is updated, the fleet is split.

What's new in v4.2.0 (October 2026)#

  • Documents (Belege): quotes, delivery notes, invoices and cancellation invoices. A new Billing tab lets the office write a quote, hand a signed delivery note to the customer on site and issue a numbered invoice — from scratch, from a quote or by combining delivery notes. See chapter 12.
  • Company profiles. Several issuing companies (name, address, UID, bank details, logo, colour, footer, signatory) can be set up; each certificate and document names the profile it was issued under (§13.3).
  • Customers carry billing details — business or private, customer number, structured address, UID (format-checked only), billing e-mail, payment term — and their detail screen lists their documents (§8).
  • Article catalogue of services and materials with unit, price and VAT rate (§13.3b).
  • Dashboard tiles for open quotes and unpaid invoices, and a Billing permission inspectors can be granted (§3, §13.6a).

Release note — update all devices together

Update every device before you create the first document on this version. v4.2.0 adds the billing tables to the shared dataset (dataset format 8). A device still on an older version cannot read a format-8 dataset: it stops syncing and says that this app version is too old for the shared data store and must be updated on this device. Nothing is lost — local work on that device continues and syncs again once it is updated — but until every device is updated, the fleet is split.

Honest limitation

The documents feature checks the mandatory contents of an Austrian invoice (§ 11 UStG 1994) before it finalises one and refuses when something is missing. It does not verify UID numbers against VIES, does not decide the VAT treatment for you, is not a cash register under the RKSV, produces no structured e-invoice (ebInterface / UBL), and stores nothing tamper-evidently. Document numbers issued on two devices while offline are detected after sync, not prevented (§12.7).

What was new in v4.1.0 (October 2026)#

  • Acceptance vs recurring inspection. Every check now records which kind of inspection it is under the Austrian AM-VO — an acceptance inspection (Abnahmeprüfung, § 7) or a recurring inspection (wiederkehrende Prüfung, § 8) — and the certificate states it. See §4.1a.
  • Try the demo. On a brand-new device the first-run screen offers a sample dataset that lives on the device only, with no Google account and no sync (§2.0).
  • Checklist gate. The checklist now applies the same completion rules as the summary and shows how many items are still open, with a jump to the next one (§4.2).
  • Reports search and filters, due-date filters on the Machines list, regrouped Settings, and an in-app link to the privacy policy (§5.1, §9, §13).
  • Forms validate as you type, mark required fields with an asterisk, and ask before you leave unsaved changes.

Release note — update all devices together

Update every device before you run the first check on this version. v4.1.0 stores the inspection kind in the shared dataset (dataset format 7). A device still on an older version cannot read a format-7 dataset: it stops syncing and says that this app version is too old for the shared data store and must be updated on this device. Nothing is lost — local work on that device continues and syncs again once it is updated — but until every device is updated, the fleet is split. Administrators: roll the update out to all devices first, then resume normal work.

1. Introduction#

1.1 What HDX Inspect does#

An inspector selects a customer and one of their machines, completes the machine's mandatory checklist (marking each item Pass, Fail or N/A), records the machine's hours or mileage and the work and travel for the visit, and captures signatures from both the inspector and the customer. The completed check is stored as a timestamped record, a numbered PDF certificate is generated in the customer's language (German or English) and filed to Google Drive, and the office or inspector then shares or prints that certificate (the app itself sends no email).

It replaces a paper-based process. The whole dataset lives in an encrypted database on each device and is shared between devices through Google Drive — there is no central server.

1.2 The two roles#

HDX Inspect has two roles. The customer is not a system user — they only sign on the inspector's device at completion and are given the PDF by your organisation.

RoleWhat they can do
Admin /
Office		Everything an inspector can do, plus: manage customers, machines and machine types; create and edit checklist templates; manage user accounts and registered devices; configure the Google Drive store; manage company profiles and certificate settings; schedule bookings; void and reissue certificates; write quotes and invoices; set the retention period; and run retention purge / device wipe.
InspectorView bookings; perform checks in the field; capture photos, machine readings, work and travel; sign and obtain the customer's sign-off; view and distribute certificates; create and sign delivery notes; resolve sync conflicts and start a sync — plus any admin capabilities an administrator has individually granted to them (§13.6a).

An administrator can grant an inspector individual admin capabilities (for example bookings, or templates) from Settings → Accounts & devices; granting all of them gives that inspector the full admin surface without changing their role. See §13.6a.

Honest limitation

Role separation is enforced in the app only — there is no server to enforce it. Anyone who has access to the configured Google Drive store can read or alter all of the underlying data regardless of their in-app role, and every inspector's device holds the whole dataset. The real access boundary is who is granted access to the Drive store, which is an administrator's responsibility (see §16).

1.3 How your data is stored and shared#

  • On each device: an encrypted local SQLite database holds the full dataset, plus your photos, signatures and cached PDFs. Everything you capture is saved locally and durably before the app confirms success.
  • Shared store: a configured Google Drive folder is the shared system of record. Devices publish their changes there and pull everyone else's. Certificates are filed under /certificates/<year>/ with a human-findable file name that leads with the customer and machine — Customer__Machine__YYYY-MM-DD__<number>.pdf — so you can spot a certificate at a glance instead of reading the bare reference number. The certificate number still trails the name (and stays on the document).
  • Sign-in vs Drive access are separate: you sign in with an app account (username and password). Google is connected separately, by an administrator, purely to give the app access to the Drive store.

1.4 Demo mode and Connected mode#

The app runs in one of two modes. The mode is normally fixed when the app is built; a Connected build can additionally be put into the demo on a device that has not been set up yet (§2.0):

  • Demo mode — local-only, seeded with sample data, with sync switched off. Google connection, the Drive store, certificate distribution and the danger-zone actions are disabled. Useful for training and trying the app.
  • Connected mode — Google Drive sync is enabled. An administrator connects Google and sets the Drive store, after which devices sync with each other.

You can tell which mode you are in from Settings → Sync & Drive: it shows either Connected mode (Backend: Google Drive) or Demo mode.

2. Getting started#

2.0 Trying the app without an account — “Try the demo”#

On a device that has not been set up yet, the Set up this device screen offers a third option, Try the demo (“Sample data on this device only. No Google account, no sync.”). Tap it to load a set of sample customers, machines, bookings and checklists onto this device and sign in as a demo administrator. Everything works as in the real app — you can run a complete inspection through to a PDF certificate — but nothing leaves the device: the sync badge reads Demo data · not synced and the Google/Drive settings are hidden.

To leave the demo, open Settings → Danger zone → Exit demo and erase sample data. This erases the sample database, every photo, signature and certificate PDF captured during the demo, and the device's database key (there is nothing to keep — the demo never syncs). A final screen then offers Close app; the next launch shows the setup chooser again. If any step fails, the app says so and nothing is reported as erased. The demo is only offered while the device has no real account.

In the demo, do not use Sign out — there is no demo password to sign back in with. If you did, close and reopen the app; it signs the demo administrator in again.

Tip

The Privacy policy and the User manual are linked at the bottom of the setup chooser and under Settings → Help & about. They open in your browser.

2.1 First run — create the first administrator#

The very first time HDX Inspect runs on a new device, there are no accounts yet, so instead of the login screen it opens a Set up this device chooser offering Set up a new organisation and Join an existing store (§2.2). For the very first device in your organisation — a brand-new store — choose Set up a new organisation; this creates the first admin account.

  1. Choose Set up a new organisation.
  2. Enter the administrator's Full name and a Username.
  3. Optionally enter an Email address.
  4. Choose a Password of at least 12 characters and type it again to confirm. It must use at least five different characters and must not contain an obvious word such as “password” or “123456”. Use the eye icon to reveal what you typed.
  5. Tap Create administrator. The account is created and you are taken straight into the app.

Strong passwords matter here

Because the account file is part of the shared dataset, anyone with Drive access could copy it and try to crack passwords offline. Always use a long, unique password.

Best practice — one account per person, created once

Create each user's account a single time, centrally, from an already-connected device (Settings → Accounts & devices, §13.6). That one account is then used on every device that person works on. Do not create a fresh account for the same person on each device — see §2.2.

2.2 Adding another device to an existing store#

Every device keeps its own encrypted local database, but they all share one Google Drive store. To bring a new device online you do not create a new set of accounts on it — you connect it to the same Drive store and let the existing accounts, customers, machines and history sync down. People then sign in with the account they already have.

On the new device, choose Join an existing store on the Set up this device screen, then work through the three steps it shows:

  1. Connect Google — sign in with the same Google account your other devices use. (This grants Drive access only; it is not your app login.)
  2. Choose the shared store — tap Find the existing store to locate the team's “HDX Inspect Data Store” folder automatically, or Enter folder ID to paste the same Drive folder ID the office already uses.
  3. Sync and sign in — tap Sync and continue: the device pulls the shared dataset, including the account roster. When it finishes you are taken to the normal sign-in screen.
  4. Sign in with your own account — the one an admin created for you centrally (§13.6). It works offline from then on.

Don't recreate accounts per device

Do not try to get “the same account on two devices” by re-creating an identical account on the new device. Accounts are matched by a hidden internal id, not by username, so a hand-made copy is a second, separate account that merely shares a name — not the same login, and it does not see the original's history. Joining the store (above) brings the real accounts down; create each person's account once (§13.6) and reuse it on every device.

Tip

One account can sign in on as many devices as a person needs, including offline. After each device syncs, they all show the same shared dataset. Joining a store needs a connection the first time, so the dataset can be pulled.

If the store turns out to be empty

If you choose Join an existing store but it holds no accounts yet — so this is really the first device in your organisation — the app tells you so and offers to set up the first administrator instead, so you are never stuck.

“No accounts yet” on a team that already has a store

If the app says the store has no accounts although your team already uses one, you are probably connected with a different Google account: Find the existing store did not find the team's folder and created a new, empty one. Go back, connect the right Google account and try again — do not set up a first administrator.

The Google account needs edit access to the store. With view-only access the app stops and asks you to have the store shared with edit access, then to join again.

2.3 Signing in#

  1. Enter your Username and Password.
  2. Tap Sign in. If the details are wrong, an error appears in red. After five wrong passwords in a row the account is locked on that device for 15 minutes.

You can sign in even with no internet connection: the app checks your details against the credentials cached on the device, so field work continues offline.

If you cannot sign in, tap Trouble signing in? below the Sign in button. It explains how password resets work (an administrator resets your password to a temporary one — see §2.4 and §13.6) and, on a connected device, offers Check for account updates: this fetches the latest synced account data, so a password reset made on another device reaches this device before you sign in. It tells you plainly if the device is not connected to Google Drive or the check fails — nothing is fetched silently.

2.3a Face ID / fingerprint or PIN sign-in (remember me)#

So you do not have to type your full password every time, HDX Inspect can remember your login on a device in one of two ways: your device biometrics (Face ID, Touch ID or a fingerprint) and/or a short device PIN. Both are optional, both are per-device, and both sit on top of your normal account — they do not replace your password.

Biometrics. On a device that has Face ID / Touch ID / a fingerprint set up, an Enable Face ID sign-in on this device option is ticked by default below the password box. Leave it ticked and sign in as normal; your login is saved on this device. Next time, tap Sign in as <your username> with Face ID (or fingerprint) and confirm with your face or finger to sign straight in.

PIN. Useful on any device — including desktops and phones without biometrics set up. On the sign-in screen tap Set PIN, choose a 4–12 digit PIN and confirm it, then sign in as usual to save it. Next time, tap Sign in with PIN and enter it. Simple PINs (all the same digit, a straight run such as 1234, and a few well-known patterns) are refused, and a PIN must not already be used by another account on the device. Five wrong PINs lock PIN sign-in on that device for 15 minutes (your password still works). You can set up either or both under Settings → Security; enabling a method there asks for your password once to confirm it is you. The biometric option is shown only on a device that has biometrics.

Shared devices with several inspectors. Each person can set up their own PIN on the same device — when you tap Sign in with PIN and type your PIN, the app knows which account it belongs to and signs you in; setting your PIN never affects anyone else's. Biometric sign-in is different: a device can remember only one account's Face ID / fingerprint at a time, so the button names whose account it will sign in to (for example, “Sign in as alice”), and turning it on for a second account asks you to confirm before it replaces the first.

What this does and does not do

Both are convenience unlocks on one device only. With biometrics, your saved login is held in the phone's secure storage and released only after your face/fingerprint is confirmed. With a PIN, your saved login is encrypted with the PIN, so the PIN is needed to recover it. Neither replaces your password: voiding or superseding a certificate, the account and device tools, the retention purge, the device wipe and deleting your account still ask you to type it, and a PIN is never accepted for those. A PIN is short by design, so it is a convenience, not a substitute for a strong password — the account password keeps its 12-character minimum because the account file is part of the shared dataset and could be attacked offline. If you change your password the biometric login updates automatically and any PIN is cleared (set a new one); if you delete your account both are removed. If your password was reset on another device, the saved Face ID / PIN login stops working here: sign in once with the new password and set it up again.

2.4 Changing your password#

First login with a temporary password. When an administrator creates your account they give you a temporary password. The first time you sign in with it, the app forces you to set your own:

  1. Re-enter the temporary password once more.
  2. Choose a new password (at least 12 characters) and confirm it.
  3. Tap Save password. You are then taken into the app.

Changing it later (voluntary). You can change your password any time from Settings → Account → Change my password. Enter your current password, then your new password twice, and confirm. The new password must be at least 12 characters and differ from the current one.

Deleting your own account. You can permanently delete your own account from Settings → Danger zone → Delete my account. The app explains what happens, then asks for your password to confirm. Deletion removes your login from every device in the organisation and signs you out; you will no longer be able to sign in. Inspection records and certificates you created are kept for the organisation — deletion removes the login, not the work. It cannot be undone. If you are the organisation's last active administrator, the app refuses, so the organisation is never left with no one in charge: create a second administrator account first (§13.6) — an existing inspector cannot be promoted in the app, and an inspector granted every permission does not count. Neither tile is shown in demo mode.

2.5 Finding your way around#

After signing in you land on the main screen. Navigation is on the left as a rail on wide screens (tablets in landscape, desktop) and along the bottom as a bar on narrow screens (phones).

On a phone the bottom bar holds every destination. They do not all fit on the screen at once, so the bar scrolls sideways: slide the bar itself to the left to bring the later destinations into view, then tap the one you want. The half-visible icon at the edge of the bar is the hint that there is more to scroll to. The bar follows the current destination, so the highlighted one is always in view. (Earlier versions showed four destinations and a More button; that button is gone.)

The bar respects your phone's font size setting: with a larger font each destination is made wide enough for its name to stay on one line, so fewer destinations are visible at once and you scroll a little further. You do not need to turn the font size down to keep the names on one line.

You can also swipe left or right across the screen content to move to the next or previous destination in the order listed below. The swipe works with a finger on phones and on tablets held in portrait, which also use the bottom bar (there all destinations usually fit without scrolling). A mouse drag across the content does not switch tabs, and the left-hand rail on wide screens is unchanged.

On a Windows PC the bottom bar appears only when the window is narrow. There you can scroll the bar with the mouse: drag the bar sideways, or turn the mouse wheel while the pointer is over the bar, then click the destination you want.

The top of every main screen shows the screen title, a ? button that opens this manual at the matching chapter (§2.7), a sync badge that reads Online, N queued, Syncing…, Offline, Sync issue (red) or N need attention (red: conflicts are waiting) — tap it to open Settings, or Sync conflicts when conflicts are waiting — and a circle with your initials (tap-and-hold shows your name and role).

The destinations are:

DestinationWhat it is forWho sees it
DashboardYour daily overview and quick actions.Everyone
BookingsThe calendar of scheduled visits.Everyone
MachinesThe machine (asset) register.Everyone
ReportsCompleted certificates.Everyone
CustomersThe customer register.Everyone
RemindersMachines that are due or overdue.Everyone
BillingQuotes, delivery notes and invoices (chapters 11–12). Called Belege in German.Everyone
TemplatesThe checklist template editor.Admin, or an inspector granted Templates
SettingsAccount, language, sync, Drive and admin tools.Everyone

2.6 Signing out#

Open Settings and tap Sign out at the bottom, then confirm. Signing out does not delete anything: your synced data remains in the Drive store and on the device. (Logging out is not the same as wiping the device — see §13.8.)

Sync only runs while someone is signed in. If the sync badge shows queued work, wait until it reads Online before signing out; otherwise that work stays on the device until the next sign-in. The Google connection is kept.

2.7 Getting help: the introduction, hints and this manual#

The app introduces itself, and help is never more than a tap away:

  • The introduction. The first time you sign in on a device, a short five-page introduction explains how to find your way around, how an inspection runs, how offline working and sync fit together, and where to find help. Swipe or tap Next to move through it, Skip to leave it at any point, and Done on the last page. Each page has a Read more in the manual link to the matching chapter.
  • Hints. After the introduction, each main screen shows a one-time hint under its title that says what the screen is for. Learn more opens the matching chapter of this manual; Got it hides the hint for good.
  • The ? button. The ? next to the sync badge at the top of every main screen opens this manual at the chapter for the screen you are on.
  • The whole manual. Settings → Help & about → User manual opens the manual from the beginning. The same link is on the first-run screen, next to the privacy policy, so you can read it before setting anything up.
  • Seeing it again. Settings → Help & about → Show the introduction again replays the introduction and brings every hint back.

The introduction and the hints are remembered per person and per device: a colleague who signs in on the same tablet gets their own introduction, and you will see it once more on a second device. Nothing about it is synced, and it never changes or blocks any of your work.

If the app was already set up on your device before this version, the introduction appears once after the update, at your next sign-in — nothing has to be set up again. Once you have finished or skipped it, it stays away: restarting the app, signing in again and later app updates do not bring it back. Only Show the introduction again, wiping the device or leaving the demo does.

Honest limitation

The manual is a web page in English, opened in your browser, and needs an internet connection — it is not stored inside the app. Without a connection the links open the browser, which then shows its own “no connection” page; the introduction and the hints themselves work offline. A PDF copy can be downloaded from the top of the manual page for offline reading.

3. The Dashboard#

The Dashboard greets you by name and gathers the things that need attention into one screen. Pull down to refresh it.

  • New check — directly under the greeting, starts an inspection (every user; §4.1). Users who may manage bookings also see New booking next to it.
  • Status cards — Overdue and Due ≤ 30 days (tap for Reminders), Bookings this week (the next seven days; tap for Bookings) and Draft checks (tap to jump to the drafts below). Overdue and Due ≤ 30 days both leave out machines that already have an open booking, so the numbers reflect real gaps.
  • Reinspection required — machines whose most recent certificate is a Blocking fail, so they must be re-inspected. A later passing check clears the machine from this list automatically. Tap it to open Reminders.
  • Today — today's visits with customer, start time and number of machines; tap one to open the booking.
  • Resume drafts — up to ten checks on this device that are not finalised yet, whoever started them. Tap a draft to carry on, or use the three-dot menu → Discard draft (with a confirmation, because it cannot be undone).
  • Recent results — the five most recently finalised checks (from any inspector); tap one to open its certificate. A voided or superseded certificate is labelled VOID / SUPERSEDED here rather than showing its old Pass/Fail result.
  • Open quotes and Unpaid invoices (users with the Billing permission) — tap either to open the Billing tab. Below them a red card appears when a finalised document still has no PDF (with a retry) or when a document number was issued twice on two devices (§12.7).
  • Attention cards appear only when something needs it: a certificate PDF that failed to generate (with Retry now), a finished inspection whose delivery note could not be created (with a retry, §11.2), or a checklist template in use that lacks item text in the working language. Opening the Dashboard re-tries pending certificates, document PDFs and delivery notes automatically.

If the Dashboard cannot load its data it shows the error with a Retry button rather than an empty screen.

Tip

A drained battery loses at most the last keystroke, never a saved answer. Every change in a check is written to the device immediately, so you can always come back to a draft from here.

4. Performing an inspection#

This is the heart of the app. A check moves through a fixed sequence of screens: select machine → checklist → machine data → summary → signatures → completion. You can leave at any point and resume later from the Dashboard or the booking.

4.1 Starting a check#

There are four ways to start:

  • From a Booking — open the booking and tap Start next to a machine (or Resume if a draft already exists). This is the normal route for planned work, and the only one that links the check to the booking (§6.2).
  • From a Reminder — book the machine first, then start it from the booking.
  • From New check on the Dashboard (every user) — pick the customer, then the machine. Each machine card shows its type, serial number and a coloured due-date chip.
  • From a machine — open it in Machines and tap Start inspection.

Whichever route you take, a sheet first asks Which inspection? — Acceptance inspection or Recurring inspection (§4.1a) — with the likely kind pre-selected and marked Suggested. Tap Continue. A machine can have only one unfinished draft: if it already has one, the sheet is skipped and that draft resumes with the kind it was started with, whichever route you take. When your store has more than one company profile, the same sheet also asks which company the check is issued under (§13.3).

When you choose a machine, the app loads its checklist — the checklist template chosen on that machine if one is set (§9.2), otherwise the machine type's default template — and copies its items onto the check, so later edits to the template never change this record. The checklist is the same for both inspection kinds.

If the machine has no checklist, or its checklist has no items yet, the check does not start and the message says what has to be added under Templates (§10).

4.1a Acceptance vs recurring inspection#

Every check records which kind of inspection it is, following the Austrian Arbeitsmittelverordnung (AM-VO):

  • Acceptance inspection (Abnahmeprüfung, § 7 AM-VO) — before a machine is first put into service, and after it has been set up at another location or substantially modified.
  • Recurring inspection (wiederkehrende Prüfung, § 8 AM-VO) — the regular periodic inspection, at least once per calendar year and at most 15 months apart.

Default rule. The sheet pre-selects Acceptance for a machine that has no recorded inspection yet, and Recurring for a machine that has been inspected before. You can always choose the other kind. On the Summary screen the kind can still be changed (next to the certificate language) until you sign; after finalisation it is fixed, like every other field of a signed check.

On the certificate. The title stays “Inspection certificate” / “Prüfzertifikat”; directly beneath it a bold line states ACCEPTANCE INSPECTION (§ 7 AM-VO) / ABNAHMEPRÜFUNG (§ 7 AM-VO) or RECURRING INSPECTION (§ 8 AM-VO) / WIEDERKEHRENDE PRÜFUNG (§ 8 AM-VO) in the certificate's language, and the first field reads Inspection type / Prüfart. Certificate numbers are unchanged — one running sequence per device covers both kinds — and so is the filing name in Drive. A small chip on checklist, machine history, booking, reports and dashboard rows shows the kind at a glance; the summary shows it as the Inspection type row.

Schedule. A passed acceptance inspection sets the machine's last-check date and next-due date exactly like a recurring inspection (the recurring interval is taken to start at commissioning); a Blocking fail on either kind brings the next-due date forward. Checks recorded before v4.1.0 count as recurring inspections.

Honest limitation

The certificate states the inspection kind as recorded by the inspector. It does not attest that the inspector holds the qualification § 7 Abs. 3 AM-VO (or any other rule) requires for that kind of inspection — that remains your organisation's responsibility. Like every other field, the kind is write-once at the application layer only; the shared store itself is not tamper-evident.

Update every device first

All devices must run the current version (v4.3.0) before the first record made on it is synchronised. An older device refuses the shared dataset loudly and keeps working locally until it is updated — nothing is lost, but it does not sync until then.

4.2 Completing the checklist#

Each item is a card numbered 1, 2, 3… with its label and (where given) a description. A header bar shows the customer, machine type and your progress (answered / total). For every item:

If the machine had any defects on its last check, a reminder banner lists them at the top of the checklist so you can confirm they have been rectified. It is informational only — it never pre-fills an answer.

  1. Tap Pass, Fail or N/A. Your choice is saved immediately.
  2. If you tap Fail, a dialog asks you to classify the defect as Blocking or Minor. The chosen severity then shows on the item as a coloured chip.
  3. Type any Notes in the field below. For a failed item the hint changes to “Describe the defect (required)…”.
  4. Add photos with the camera button. On a phone or tablet you can take a photo or choose from the gallery; on desktop you pick a file. Tap a thumbnail to mark it up (see below). To delete a photo, tap the small × on it or long-press it; the app asks you to confirm. A small brush badge on a thumbnail means it has been annotated.

Tapping the answer you already selected clears it again. A photo-required item says so under its photos, and its camera button stays amber until it has one.

The header shows your progress and, while anything is still missing, an orange N open issues chip; the Continue — machine data button stays disabled and names the same count. Tap the chip or Next open item to jump straight to the first item that needs attention (it is highlighted briefly), or switch on Only open items to hide everything already complete. Answered items colour their Pass / Fail / N/A button green / red / grey so a list can be scanned at a glance. When every rule is met, tap Continue — machine data.

Marking up a photo

Tap a photo to open the annotation editor and point out a defect on the image itself. You can draw freehand, or add an arrow, rectangle, ellipse or a short text tag, in any of five colours. Undo removes the last mark, Clear removes them all, then tap Save. A photo takes up to 200 marks, and a text tag up to 200 characters.

Annotations are non-destructive: the original photo is never altered — the marks are stored separately and drawn onto a flattened copy that is baked into the certificate when the check is finalised. You can only annotate a draft; once a check is signed off its photos are fixed.

Validation rules (these are strict)

The app will not let you finalise a check unless the rules below are met — it never quietly passes an item for you:

• A Fail requires a defect classification (Blocking or Minor), a non-empty note, and at least one photo.

• Every item must be explicitly answered. An unanswered item blocks completion.

• On a photo-required item, a Pass needs at least one photo — or, if a photo is genuinely impossible in the field, a note explaining why. An N/A needs an explanatory note.

The checklist applies exactly the same rules as the summary and the final sign-off — so what the checklist lets through, the summary accepts. If a photo-required item has no photo, supply the photo whenever you can; where that is impossible, record the reason in the item's note so the check can still be completed. A failed item always needs a photo. While a photo is being saved, its camera button shows a spinner. Notes are saved a moment after you stop typing; Continue waits for that save to finish, and if a note could not be saved on the device it tells you and stays on the checklist rather than moving on with an unsaved note. Leaving with Back waits for the save in the same way; if a note still cannot be saved you choose between Retry, Discard and leave (the last saved text is kept) and Stay — a typed note is never dropped silently.

Defect severity drives the result

Blocking means the machine fails and a reinspection is required — its next-due date is brought forward. Minor means “Pass with defects”: the defect is recorded and carried forward to the next check, with the normal next-due date.

4.3 Recording machine data#

The Machine data & time screen captures meter readings and the visit's work and travel. Which reading fields appear depends on what the machine type tracks:

  • Operating hours — shown and required if the type tracks hours (entered in hours, with a decimal point or comma).
  • Odometer (km) — shown if the type tracks kilometres.
  • If the type tracks neither, the app says so rather than storing a hidden zero.
  • Work time, Travel time and Travel distance — these become the lines of the visit's delivery note when the inspection is finalised (chapter 11). Times are entered in decimal hours (1.5 = 1 h 30 min).

The reading fields start with the machine's last recorded values — overwrite them with today's reading. Negative values are rejected. If a reading is lower than the last one recorded for that machine, the app warns you and asks for a reason (for example a replaced meter) before it accepts it with Use this reading. Without a reason the reading is not accepted and the check cannot be finalised — a lower reading is never silently taken or thrown away. Tap Continue — summary when done.

4.4 Reviewing the summary#

The Summary screen shows the overall result as a coloured banner — green PASS, amber PASS — MINOR DEFECTS, or red FAIL — together with a count of passed / minor / blocking / N/A items, the customer and machine details, the date, the readings and the work/travel figures. Any failed items are listed with their severity and notes. While something still needs attention, an orange banner is shown instead of the result, and the button at the bottom is disabled and names the reason (for example “2 items unanswered” or “Translation required”) instead of Sign & complete — tap the banner to go back to the checklist, which scrolls to the first open item.

Certificate language

The summary carries a Certificate language control (Deutsch / English). The check starts in the customer's preferred language (§8.1), and you can switch it here up until you sign — after that it is fixed. This sets the language of the whole PDF certificate; it is independent of the app's own interface language (§13.1).

Honest limitation

A certificate can only be finalised if the checklist has text in the certificate's language for every item. If some items have not been translated into that language, the app blocks finalisation and says so rather than issuing a half-translated certificate — switch the certificate to the other language, or have an administrator add the missing template text (§10). This works both ways: an English certificate needs English text, a German certificate needs German text.

Important — read this

Once you sign, the certificate is locked and cannot be edited. After that, a mistake can only be put right by an administrator voiding or superseding the certificate (§5.4–5.5) — never by editing it. Check the summary carefully before signing.

4.5 Signatures#

Tapping Sign & complete collects two signatures in turn on the device's signature pad. Draw with a finger or stylus; use Undo to remove the last stroke or Clear to start again, then tap Confirm.

  1. Inspector signature — you sign first.
  2. Customer sign-off — the customer enters their name and signs, confirming the declaration shown above the signature pad: that the inspection was performed and the results, including any defects found, were presented to them.

If the customer cannot or will not sign

Tap Customer cannot sign on the customer signature screen (or dismiss it) and the app asks why, offering Customer unavailable or Customer refused to sign with an optional note. The check is then finalised with your signature and the recorded reason — it is never silently treated as signed.

4.6 Completion and the certificate#

After signing, the check is finalised and the certificate is produced:

  • On success you see Inspection completed, the result banner, and a View certificate button. Tap Done to return to the app.
  • If the PDF could not be generated, you see Certificate pending with a Retry certificate button. The check itself is finalised — only the PDF needs another attempt. The app retries automatically whenever the Dashboard opens, and the Dashboard shows a red card with Retry now until it succeeds.
  • When the check recorded work or travel, the screen also offers Delivery note: review and sign (chapter 11).

A check is operationally complete when it is finalised, its certificate is generated, and the record, photos and PDF have synced to Drive. The app sends nothing to the customer by itself: you share or print the certificate from Reports (§5.3). Sending it is separate and is never required for the work to count as complete — so a forgotten send never means lost work.

5. Reports & certificates#

5.1 The reports list#

Reports lists every completed, signed-off check, newest first (pull to refresh). Each row shows the machine, the customer, date and certificate number, the inspection-kind chip (§4.1a), a Pass/Minor/Fail chip, and the distribution status (Not yet distributed, or Handed off with the date). On a voided or superseded certificate the machine name is struck through and the result chip is replaced by a grey VOID / SUPERSEDED chip.

Use the search box to find a certificate by customer, machine or certificate number, and the filter chips to narrow the list by result (Pass / Minor defects / Fail), to voided or superseded certificates only, by inspection kind (Acceptance / Recurring) or by a date range; Clear filters resets them. The list loads the newest 300 certificates; when there are more, a footer says so and Load more extends it. Search and filters cover the certificates loaded so far — tap Load more to include older ones.

5.2 Viewing a certificate#

Tap a report to open the full PDF certificate. You can pinch to zoom and swipe through pages, and use the standard Print and Share controls. A red banner appears across the top if the certificate has been VOIDed or SUPERSEDED; the original is always retained for the record. If the signed original is not on this device and cannot be downloaded, the app shows a regenerated preview and says so in a banner — it is not the signed original; sync and reopen to get that.

The certificate's header, logo, banner image and accent colour come from the company profile it was issued under (Settings → Company profiles, §13.3), and the declaration wording from Settings → Certificate settings (§13.3a). Each certificate keeps the branding it was issued with, so later rebrands never change certificates already issued.

5.3 Distributing a certificate#

Distribution is a deliberate manual handoff. From the certificate view, the Record distribution action notes that you have handed the report off, and you use Share / Print to actually send it (for example, attaching the PDF to an email from your own mailbox or saving it). A handoff can be recorded only once the certificate and its photos have synced to the Drive store; until then the app says the evidence is still syncing. In Demo mode recording a handoff is switched off.

Honest limitation

The app records a handoff, not a delivery. It cannot prove a customer received a report, so the status reads “Handed off — delivery not confirmed”, never “delivered”. Because the filed PDF is the system of record, a forgotten or failed send loses nothing — each row in Reports shows Not yet distributed until a handoff is recorded. The app sends no email itself.

5.4 Voiding a certificate (Admin, or the Certificates permission)#

Use Void when a certificate was issued in error. Voiding keeps the original and clearly marks it VOID. Because a voided certificate no longer counts, the machine's due date is recalculated from its remaining valid certificates (so a voided Blocking-fail no longer leaves the machine stuck overdue). It is recorded in the audit log and cannot be undone.

  1. Open the certificate and tap the Void certificate icon in the title bar.
  2. Enter a reason (required), e.g. “issued in error”.
  3. Re-enter your own password when prompted (destructive actions require it).
  4. The certificate is re-stamped VOID and the change syncs to Drive.

The two icons are visible to every user; whether you may use them is checked after you enter the reason. Without the permission the app says that only an admin, or a user granted the certificates permission, can perform the action.

5.5 Superseding / reissuing (Admin, or the Certificates permission)#

Use Supersede when a corrected certificate replaces an earlier one. Both are kept and linked, and the old one is marked SUPERSEDED.

  1. Produce the replacement check/certificate for the same machine.
  2. Open the original certificate and tap the Mark superseded icon in the title bar, and enter a reason.
  3. Pick the replacement from the list of that machine's other finalised certificates (voided ones are left out). Entries are identified by their date and result, not by certificate number. Confirm with Supersede.
  4. Re-enter your own password when prompted. The original is marked SUPERSEDED and linked to the replacement; the change syncs.

Like a void, a supersede recalculates the machine's due date from its remaining valid certificates. A superseded certificate can still be voided; a voided one cannot be superseded.

Corrections are append-only

Finalised checks are never edited in place. The only corrections are a void or a supersede — each retained and logged.

6. Bookings & scheduling#

The office plans work through a calendar of bookings. A booking is one customer visit: it links a customer, one or more machines, an assigned inspector, a start and end time, and a status. Each machine on the booking produces its own check and certificate.

6.1 The calendar#

Move between months with the arrows; days with bookings carry a dot and today is outlined. Tap a day to see its bookings below the calendar. Each booking card shows the customer, the start time, how many machines are on the visit, the assigned inspector and a status chip. Tap the card to open the booking: its time, notes and the list of machines. Cancelled bookings are no longer shown on the calendar.

6.2 Starting work from a booking#

Next to each machine on a booking is a Start button — or Resume if a draft check already exists, or a green tick if that machine's check is already finalised. Tapping it takes you straight into the checklist for that machine. A booking is completed when every machine on it is finalised.

Start from the booking

Start planned work from the booking. A check started from New check on the Dashboard or from the machine's own screen is not linked to the booking: it neither moves the booking to In progress nor counts towards completing it.

6.3 Creating or editing a booking (Admin, or the Bookings permission)#

Administrators, and inspectors granted the Bookings permission, tap Edit booking in an open booking, or create one with the “+” button on Bookings, New booking on the Dashboard or Book in Reminders. Everyone else sees the calendar read-only. The booking form:

  1. Choose the Customer (required) — this filters the machine list.
  2. Tick the Machines for the visit (at least one).
  3. Optionally assign an Inspector (or leave Unassigned).
  4. Set the Date, Start time and End time (09:00–12:00 by default; the end must be after the start).
  5. When editing an existing booking, set the Status: Planned, In progress, Completed, Cancelled or Rescheduled. A new booking is always Planned. Starting a check from the booking moves it to In progress automatically, and finalising the last machine's check moves it to Completed — you rarely need to set those by hand.
  6. Add Notes for site access, contacts, etc., then tap Save booking.

When you change a booking's date, time or assigned inspector, the previous values are recorded in the audit log so the history of a rescheduled or reassigned visit is preserved.

7. Reminders — due & overdue#

Reminders lists machines that need a booking so nothing falls through the gaps. A machine that already has an open (planned, in-progress or rescheduled) booking is left off the list — it is already scheduled. It has two sections:

  • Overdue — machines past their next-due date with no booking (red), sorted by how overdue they are.
  • Due within 30 days — machines coming due soon with no booking (amber).

Each machine shows its name, customer and a coloured due chip. If you may manage bookings, tap Book on a machine to open the booking form pre-filled with that customer and machine, so scheduling the visit is one step. When nothing is due the screen says that nothing is due in the next 30 days. Pull down to refresh.

A machine that has never been inspected has no due date and does not appear here — find it in Machines.

A machine's next-due date is computed from the issue date of its last completed check plus its re-check interval (defaulted from the machine type, overridable per machine). A Blocking failure brings the next-due date forward.

8. Customers#

Customers is the register of the organisations you inspect for. Search by name, and toggle Show archived to include archived records. Tap a customer to see their details and the machines registered to them.

8.1 Creating or editing a customer (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

Administrators, and inspectors granted the Customers & machines permission, add a customer with the “+” button, or edit one from its detail screen. A customer record carries the company name, a contact name and phone, a report email, the address, notes and a preferred certificate language (Deutsch or English). New checks for the customer start in that language, and it can still be changed per check up until finalisation (§4.4). New customers default to the organisation's default language (set in Settings → Certificate settings, §13.3a).

A customer that anything refers to — machines, bookings, inspections or documents — cannot be deleted, only archived, so historical certificates stay resolvable; the app offers Archive instead. Archiving a customer also archives its machines, and Restore brings both back. A customer that nothing refers to can be removed with the three-dot menu → Delete permanently.

E-mail addresses are for your reference

The Report email and the Billing e-mail are kept on the customer record for your reference. The app does not send e-mail and does not pre-fill a recipient: when you share a PDF, you enter the address in your own mail app.

8.2 Billing details and the customer's documents#

Since v4.2.0 the customer form also carries what a quote or invoice needs: whether the customer is a business (Firma) or a private person (Privat — salutation, first and last name), a customer number (unique among live customers), a structured address (street, postcode, city, country) used on documents, the UID number, a separate billing e-mail, a default payment term, a default reference line, the document language, a contact line on documents (business customers) and internal billing notes. Payment term and document language can be left on company default. An Austrian postcode must have four digits. The older free-text address is shown, read-only, only until you fill in the structured address.

If two devices gave the same customer number to different customers while apart, the list shows a red notice naming the numbers after sync; renumber one. The app never merges or deletes customers by itself.

UID numbers are format-checked, not verified

The UID number is checked for format only (Austrian UIDs must be ATU + 8 digits; those of other countries are checked only for their general shape). The app does not query the EU VIES service and cannot tell you whether a UID is valid or belongs to this customer. Verify it yourself where the VAT treatment depends on it (reverse charge, intra-Community supply).

Below the customer's details, a Documents (Belege) section lists their quotes, delivery notes and invoices with number, date and status, above the customer's machines. For an active customer it offers New quote / New delivery note / New invoice buttons (the quote and invoice buttons need the Billing permission).

9. Machines & machine types#

The Machines list has a search box plus Overdue and Due soon filter chips and a Sort by due date toggle (soonest first; machines without a due date last).

9.1 The machine register#

Machines lists every machine (asset). Search by name, serial or customer. Each row shows the machine type icon, the display name, the customer, the serial number and a due-date chip. Tap a machine to see its detail: customer, type, serial, year, due date, current hours/km, last check, interval and whether auto-booking is on, plus a Start inspection button and the machine's History — every check on it. Tap a finished check in the history to open its certificate, or a draft to continue it.

9.2 Creating or editing a machine (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

  1. Tap “+” on Machines (or Edit on a machine's detail).
  2. Choose the Customer and the Machine type from the icon tiles (both required; the first type is pre-selected on a new machine, and the New type tile creates a type without leaving the form).
  3. Fill in the Label / fleet name, Make, Model, Serial number and Year (1900–2100) as available.
  4. Set the Inspection interval override (months) only if this machine differs from its type's default.
  5. Switch on Auto-book next check if the next visit should be booked automatically (see below).
  6. Leave Checklist template on Default for type unless this machine needs its own checklist. A template whose items lack text in the working language cannot be chosen.
  7. Tap Save.

Auto-book next check

When this switch is on, finalising a check creates the next visit automatically: a Planned booking without an inspector at 08:00 on the machine's new next-due date, noted as an auto-booked re-check, which the office then adjusts. A future visit you have already planned for the machine is never doubled. Because the machine then has an open booking, it stays off the Reminders list.

9.3 Machine types (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

The icon button next to the Machines search box opens Machine types (e.g. Crane, Forklift, Tractor). Each type carries a default checklist template, a default re-check interval, and whether it tracks operating hours and/or kilometres. Creating a type lets you set its name, default interval, the tracked readings, and — ticked by default — create its (empty) checklist template at the same time. Tapping a type opens it for editing (name, default interval, tracked readings); its checklist is edited under Templates (chapter 10).

The list warns on a type that has no default checklist or whose checklist is empty: checks for machines of that type cannot start until that is put right under Templates.

10. Checklist templates (Admin)#

Templates (administrators, and inspectors granted the Templates permission) is where the checklists themselves are built. A template belongs to a machine type. A type can have several templates: one is the type's default, and any other can be assigned to individual machines in the machine form (§9.2). The list shows the type, the version and a default, standard or archived tag under each name.

10.1 Creating and editing a template#

To create a template, tap “+” on Templates, give it a name, choose its machine type and tap Create; the editor opens.

Open a template to edit its items. Each item has a check description (its label), optional guidance / acceptance criteria, and a photo-required flag. Add an item with + Item and edit one by tapping it; each item is saved with Save in its own sheet. The bin icon on a row deletes the item after a confirmation (past checks keep their own copy). To reorder, drag an item by the handle at its right edge, then tap Save order in the bar that appears — the new order is not saved until you do. To rename the template, tap the pencil icon in the title bar — the new name applies to lists and future editing only; checks already performed are unaffected.

To make a template the default checklist for its machine type, open it and tap the star icon in the title bar (Set as default for type). The app refuses while any item has no text in the working language.

An optional item interval in months can be recorded on an item. It is informational for now: it is shown on the item but does not yet change which items a check contains.

Each item can carry its text in both languages. You author in the organisation's working language first (the default language set in Settings → Certificate settings, §13.3a) — that field is required. The other language is optional: you can add it now or leave it blank. A German-first organisation therefore never has to type English it does not use.

If you leave the other language blank

The editor shows a small notice listing any items that have no text in the other language. That is not an error — the template still works. It only means a certificate issued in that language will be blocked at sign-off for those items until their text is added (§4.4). Certificates in the working language are unaffected.

10.2 Versioning#

How template versions behave

Each check copies the template's items when it is started, so editing a template later never alters historical or in-progress checks. The template's version number goes up each time it is edited; the template itself is not frozen.

Templates are archived, never hard-deleted. A checklist template assigned to a machine takes precedence over the type's default for that machine.

10.3 Archiving a template you no longer need#

To remove a template from the list, open it, tap the three-dot menu at the right of the title bar and choose Archive template, then confirm. The template disappears from the Templates list and can no longer be chosen for machines or new checks. Past checks and certificates are unaffected: each keeps its own copy of the checklist.

  • Still in use? Archiving is refused while the template is a machine type's default checklist or the checklist template of an active machine. The message names the reason: set another default for the type (the star icon, §10.1), or choose another checklist template on those machines, then archive.
  • Changed your mind? Tap Show archived templates at the bottom of the Templates list, open the template and choose Restore template from the three-dot menu.
  • Unsaved item order? Archive stays unavailable until you save or discard a changed item order.
  • Inactive machines that use an archived template keep it. Their machine form shows it marked archived, and saving the form does not change it.

11. Work & travel → delivery notes#

The work hours, travel time and travel distance an inspector records on the Machine data & time step (§4.3) are not collected on a separate screen any more. When the inspection is finalised, the app adds them to a delivery note (Lieferschein) automatically — the same figures, now on the document the customer signs for.

11.1 What happens at completion#

  • One line per recorded figure — work time in hours, travel time in hours (two decimals) and distance in kilometres (one decimal). Each line is headed by the name of the company profile's default article for work, travel or distance (§13.3), followed by Inspection <machine type> <machine> – Certificate <number> – <date>, so the invoice built later is already priced. If no default article is set, the line is created without an article at price 0 — set the price on the invoice. The delivery note itself prints no prices.
  • One note per visit. If a draft delivery note already exists for the same customer, issuing company and day, the new inspection's lines are appended to it. A job with several machines ends with one note. Otherwise a new draft is created. A note that was already finalised is never changed — a later inspection on the same day starts a new draft.
  • The note stays a draft. The completion screen offers Delivery note: review and sign: it opens the draft in the editor where you check the lines and finalise (this allocates the number, §12.4); then choose the three-dot menu → Sign to take the customer's signature on the device (§12.5). You can also do that later from the Billing tab, where the draft is listed like any other.
  • Nothing recorded, no note. An inspection without work, travel or distance figures creates no delivery note. An inspection is never put on a second note.
  • Your edits stick. If you remove an inspection's lines from the draft — say its travel is already on the sibling machine's line, or you replace the automatic lines with one agreed line — the app does not put them back. Only voiding the finalised note or discarding the draft frees its inspections, so a fresh note can be created for them.

11.2 If the note could not be created#

Creating the note never holds up the inspection: the certificate is issued and the record locked first. If the note cannot be created (for example no company profile has been set up yet), the completion screen says so instead of showing the button, and the app retries the next time the dashboard loads. While an inspection is still waiting for its note, the dashboard shows a warning with the count and a Retry now button; it disappears once the note has been created. The attempt is recorded in the activity log. Inspections completed before this version was installed on the device are not turned into notes — only inspections finalised from then on.

Honest limitation

The automatic note is a convenience in the app, not an enforcement. Travel is recorded per inspection, so a visit covering several machines lists each machine's travel — remove the duplicates in the editor before you finalise. If two devices finalise inspections of the same visit before they have synced, each may hold its own draft note; both are visible in the Billing tab and either can be discarded. Any user can discard a draft note; voiding a finalised one needs the Billing permission.

11.3 Work & travel CSV export#

The spreadsheet export of recorded work and travel is on the Billing tab → Delivery notes list: tap Export CSV. It covers the completed inspections in the list's date filter (the current month when no range is set), one row per inspection with its date, customer, machine, inspector, work hours, travel hours, distance and result, and hands the file to the share sheet (mail, Drive, Files…). If the share sheet cannot be opened, the app saves the file and copies its location to the clipboard. The CSV is injection-hardened (cells that could be read as formulas are neutralised). It is independent of the delivery notes themselves and available to every signed-in user.

12. Documents — quotes, delivery notes & invoices#

The Billing tab (Belege in German; some messages in the app call it Documents) is where the office writes quotes (Angebote), delivery notes (Lieferscheine), invoices (Rechnungen) and cancellation invoices (Stornorechnungen). It follows the same offline-first rules as the rest of the app: everything is saved on the device as you work and syncs to the Drive store when connected. Documents are bilingual — each one is written in German or English, following the customer's document language.

The tab has three lists: Quotes, Delivery notes and Invoices (cancellation invoices appear under Invoices). Each list has a search box (number, customer or reference), status chips, a date range, a company filter when there is more than one profile, and Clear filters; Load more extends a list beyond its first 50 rows.

Every signed-in user sees the Billing tab and can write and sign delivery notes. Quotes, invoices, cancellation invoices and the article catalogue need the Billing permission, which administrators hold and can grant to an inspector (§13.6a); without it, quote and invoice drafts open view-only. Company profiles are edited with the Organisation settings permission (§13.3).

12.1 Before the first invoice: the company profile#

An invoice must name its issuer in full. Open Settings → Company profiles (§13.3) and complete the default profile — name, address, UID number, and bank details if you want them in the page footer and the EPC QR code printed. Finalising an invoice is refused while the issuer's name, address or UID is missing (a small-business-exempt invoice may omit the UID; for that treatment switch on Small business scheme on the profile first). If you move over from another system mid-year, set the number floor per document type so numbering continues where you left off.

12.2 Creating a document#

  • From the Billing tab — open the Quotes, Delivery notes or Invoices list and tap New quote / New delivery note / New invoice. The editor opens with the default company; choose the Customer (and another Issuing company if needed) at the top. Without the Billing permission the button appears on Delivery notes only.
  • From a customer — the New quote / delivery note / invoice buttons on the customer's detail screen (§8.2).
  • From a quote — an open or accepted quote offers Create delivery note and Create invoice; the lines are copied (optional quote lines are left out) and the new document links back to the quote.
  • From delivery notes — tick several open or signed notes of one customer and company in the list and tap Create invoice from N delivery notes: one combined invoice with a group per note and the service period spanning them. For a single note, open it and choose the three-dot menu → Create invoice. The invoice takes the customer's default payment term (else the company's) and its due date; the notes themselves carry none. The notes become Verrechnet (invoiced) when that invoice is finalised.

The result is always a draft (Entwurf) that opens in the editor. A draft has no number, can be edited or discarded freely, and can be shared only as a preview that shows a red Entwurf / Draft in place of the number.

12.3 The editor#

A new document needs a customer before it is saved

Choose the customer first. A new document is stored only once it has a customer. From then on every change is saved on the device within a moment, and the editor flushes before Preview, Finalise and Back. If you leave a new document before choosing a customer, nothing is kept and the app does not warn you.

Add customer beside the Customer field creates a customer without leaving the editor. The fields depend on the type:

  • Document date (not in the future), reference / order number, and the customer's document language and VAT treatment (standard; reverse charge for construction services § 19 Abs. 1a or general § 19 Abs. 1; intra-Community supply Art. 6 Abs. 1; small-business exemption § 6 Abs. 1 Z 27; export; other exemption with your own reason text).
  • Quotes: a valid-until date. Delivery notes: the delivery date (required). Invoices: the service date or period (required by § 11 UStG) and Delivery note number(s), filled in automatically when the invoice is built from delivery notes.
  • Payment term on quotes and invoices: 8, 14, 21 or 30 days net, On receipt, or No payment term. An invoice's Due on date follows from it and can be adjusted by hand. A cancellation invoice has no payment term, and its company and customer are fixed.
  • Opening and closing text, filled in once when the document is created, from the profile's texts for that type and language (or the built-in wording); internal notes that are never printed. If you change the document language afterwards, check the opening and closing text — it is not replaced.
  • Lines: Add from article (name, unit, price and VAT rate are copied, then editable) or Add free text. Each line has a description, quantity (up to three decimals), unit, net unit price, an optional discount in %, a VAT rate, an optional machine and an optional note; delivery-note lines have no price, discount or VAT fields. Quotes can mark a line optional (printed, not totalled); combined invoices show a group label per delivery note. Drag to reorder.
  • The totals (net, VAT per rate, gross) update live; amounts are calculated in cents and rounded half-away-from-zero per line and per VAT group.

VAT treatment is your decision

Choosing a reverse-charge or exempt treatment forces every line to 0 % VAT and prints the corresponding statutory note on the document (English documents print the English wording with the German original beneath). Reverse charge and intra-Community supply require the customer's UID (a non-Austrian one for intra-Community supply). The app checks these rules; it does not tell you which treatment applies.

12.4 Finalising: number, snapshot, PDF#

Finalise (Fertigstellen) checks the document and, if everything is in place, allocates its number and locks it. Numbers have the form YYYYNNNN — the year of the document date followed by a sequence that restarts each year and runs separately per company profile and per type (quotes, delivery notes, invoices and cancellation invoices each have their own sequence). The next number is the highest one already issued plus one, or the configured floor.

Finalising is refused — with a list of what is missing. Every document needs a customer name, a document date that is not in the future, and at least one line that is not optional; every line needs a description, a quantity other than zero and a price that is not negative; a delivery note needs its delivery date.

Invoices and cancellation invoices are additionally refused when: the issuer's name, address or UID is incomplete; the customer has no usable address; there is no service date or period, or the period ends before it starts; the gross total exceeds € 10,000 and the customer has no UID (§ 11 Abs. 1 Z 2 UStG); a UID does not have a recognisable format; a reverse-charge or intra-Community document lacks the customer's UID, or an intra-Community supply the issuer's; a non-standard treatment still has lines with VAT; the small-business treatment is chosen but the profile's Small business scheme switch is off; an “other exemption” has no reason text; or the company profile has been archived.

  • At finalisation the document snapshots the issuer (from the company profile) and the recipient (from the customer record). Later edits to the profile or the customer never change an issued document.
  • A finalised document is write-once at the application layer: the app refuses every edit to it, locally and when another device's change arrives through sync. Corrections are made by cancellation invoice or void (§12.5), never in place.
  • The PDF is rendered right after the record is locked. If rendering fails (for example the app is closed at that moment) the document stays finalised and numbered and is marked PDF pending. Opening the Billing tab retries it for every user and shows a notice with Retry; users with the Billing permission also see a red card on the Dashboard until it succeeds. The finished PDF is filed in the Drive store under /documents/‹company›/‹year›/ and its hash is stored on the record.
  • On a second device a quote, delivery note or invoice renders without the logo or banner if that image has not yet synced to the device; sync first when the header matters. (A certificate in the same situation stays pending until the image arrives.)

Invoices finalise online

In Connected mode the app syncs first before it finalises an invoice or cancellation invoice, so the number it allocates is based on the freshest data this device can see. If the store cannot be reached, finalising an invoice is refused and the app asks you to connect and sync, then try again — finalise it when you are back online. Quotes and delivery notes finalise offline. Even so, two devices finalising while apart can still issue the same number; this is detected afterwards, see §12.7.

12.5 Statuses and what you can do next#

TypeStatusesActions
QuoteDraft (Entwurf) → Open (Offen) → Accepted (Angenommen) / Rejected (Abgelehnt); Void (Ungültig)Accept or reject; create a delivery note or an invoice from it (open or accepted); void with a reason.
Delivery noteDraft → Open → Signed (Unterschrieben) → Invoiced (Verrechnet); VoidSign on the device (customer signature with name, or record that the customer could not sign and why); combine into an invoice; void while open and unsigned.
InvoiceDraft → Open → Paid (Bezahlt); Cancelled (Storniert); VoidMark paid (date, method, note); cancel with a cancellation invoice; void only while unshared.
Cancellation invoiceDraft → OpenTerminal — it cannot be cancelled or voided itself.

The English interface shows the English status names, the German interface the German ones. The actions are in the three-dot menu of an open document. Mark sent (your own attestation that you sent it) is available on every finalised document that is not void, for users with the Billing permission. The document view also lists its linked documents, signatures and activity, and when it reached the shared store, was shared from the app or was marked sent.

  • Signing a delivery note (or accepting a quote by signature) adds a dated recipient signature (or the recorded waiver) and re-renders the PDF with the signature image above the recipient line; the previous PDF is kept. Signed and invoiced notes can no longer be voided. If you record that the customer could not sign, the reason is stored, the note stays Open (so it can still be voided) and no signature can be added afterwards. A device that has the signature record but not yet its image keeps the document PDF pending rather than produce a PDF with an empty signature box; it renders after the next sync brings the image.
  • Mark paid records the payment date, method (bank transfer, cash, card, other) and a note. Paying by cash shows a reminder that this app is not a cash register: an RKSV-compliant receipt must be issued from a registered cash register where the law requires one.
  • Cancellation invoice (Stornorechnung): the correct way to undo an invoice that has been shared or paid. It is a new numbered document with the negative amounts and the original's issuer and recipient, states the reason, links to the original and sets it to Cancelled / Storniert when finalised. Cancel invoice asks for a reason and your password and opens the cancellation invoice as a draft; the original changes only when you finalise that draft. Issue a corrected invoice afterwards as a new document.
  • Void (Ungültig) is for a document that was never sent — it needs the Billing permission, a reason and your password, and the PDF is re-rendered with a VOID banner. The record and its number are retained; the number is not reused. The app refuses to void an invoice that was shared or printed from the app; for quotes and open delivery notes it does not check, so void them only if they never left the building.
  • Discard removes a draft (and only a draft) after confirmation. Any user can discard a draft delivery note.

12.6 Preview, share and print#

Every document opens a PDF preview. Drafts preview with a red Entwurf / Draft in place of the number. Finalised documents show the stored PDF (verified against its stored hash). Share / print hands the PDF to another app — e-mail, messenger, printer — under a file name like Rechnung_20260042.pdf; the document records that it was shared. For an invoice or cancellation invoice the Share / print button stays disabled until the record has synced to the Drive store once, so no number leaves the device before every other device can see it (immediate in Demo mode) — a Sync now button appears beside it while it waits. The button is also disabled while a number collision affects the document, for a voided document, and while the PDF is still pending.

The printed invoice carries everything § 11 UStG asks for — issuer and recipient, number, date, service period, quantities and descriptions, net amounts per VAT rate, VAT amounts, gross total, the issuer's UID and, where required, the customer's UID and the statutory note for the treatment — plus the payment term and due date. Bank name, IBAN and BIC print in the page footer when the profile's footer lines are empty (§13.3); a finalised invoice with a positive total also carries an EPC QR code (if the profile has an IBAN) that banking apps scan to pre-fill the transfer.

12.7 Number collisions between devices#

Google Drive cannot reserve a number for one device. If two devices finalise, say, an invoice each while both are offline, both can allocate the same number. When the records meet during sync the app detects the duplicate: a red banner appears on the Dashboard and in the Billing lists, both documents are marked, and neither can be shared or printed — nor is either filed to /documents/ in Drive — until it is resolved. The app never renumbers a document by itself — a number that has been printed must not change silently. To resolve it, decide which document stands, void the other and issue it again; the new number continues after the highest in use. Finalising invoices online (§12.4) makes this rare, not impossible.

Honest limitation

In the current version only a void lifts the block. If the document to withdraw was already shared it can only be cancelled with a cancellation invoice, and the collision notice then stays on both documents. If that happens, keep the paperwork of both and speak to your administrator.

Honest limitation

Numbering across devices is detected after sync, not prevented. Unlike certificate numbers, document numbers carry no device prefix because Austrian practice expects one consecutive sequence per company; the pre-finalise sync, the share gate and the collision banner are the mitigations.

12.8 What the documents feature does not do#
