  • It does not verify UID numbers (no VIES query) and does not decide the VAT treatment.
  • It is not a cash register under the RKSV — cash receipts are not signed, chained or exported as DEP.
  • It produces PDF only — no ebInterface / UBL e-invoice, no accounting (BMD) export.
  • Numbered documents are write-once by the app's behaviour; nothing in the Drive store is tamper-evident.
  • Retention (§ 132 BAO, seven years) and the handover to your accountant remain operator tasks; the PDFs live in the Drive store under /documents/.

13. Settings#

Settings holds your profile, the language toggle, the Google/Drive connection, sync status and the administrator tools. What you see depends on your role and on whether the app is in Connected or Demo mode. Since v4.1.0 the screen is grouped under headings — Account, Appearance & language, Sync & Drive, Security, Administration (now including Company profiles, Articles and Certificate settings), Help & about and Danger zone. For a user who holds no administrator permission, the Administration tiles are folded into one collapsed Administration entry (branding and the audit log stay viewable; locked tiles explain why when tapped). Help & about shows the app version and company and holds the Privacy policy, the User manual and Show the introduction again (§2.7). Delete my account lives in the Danger zone with the other irreversible actions; in a “Try the demo” session the Danger zone holds Exit demo and erase sample data instead (§2.0), and the Security group, Change my password and Delete my account are hidden.

13.1 Profile and language#

The top card shows your name, email and role. Below it, the Language toggle switches the app's interface between English and German, taking effect immediately. This is a per-device preference: it applies to everyone who signs in on that device. A freshly installed app starts in German on a German-language device and in English otherwise.

Interface language vs certificate language

The Language toggle here changes only what you see on screen. The language a certificate is printed in is a separate setting that follows the customer (§8.1) and can be adjusted per check on the summary screen until it is signed (§4.4). So an English-speaking inspector can still produce a German certificate, and vice versa.

13.2 Appearance — light & dark mode#

The Appearance control sets how the app looks on this device: System (follow the device's own light/dark setting), Light, or Dark. It takes effect immediately.

Appearance is a per-device preference — it is not synced to your other devices, and it has no effect on certificates or exports, which always render the same way regardless of the theme you use.

13.3 Company profiles (Admin / Organisation settings)#

Company profiles (Firmenprofile) describe the companies you issue certificates and documents under. Every store has one default profile; until an administrator edits it, it carries the organisation's certificate company name and logo, so existing certificates look exactly as before. Add further profiles when you invoice from more than one company. Everyone can view the profiles; editing them needs the Organisation settings permission, which administrators hold (the Billing permission alone shows them read-only). The list has an Add company profile button, an icon to show archived profiles, and a three-dot menu per profile with Set as default and Archive. A profile holds:

  • Display name, legal name, street, postcode, city, phone, e-mail and UID number — the issuer block of every document, and what § 11 UStG requires an invoice to show.
  • Bank name, IBAN and BIC — printed in the page footer of documents when you leave the footer lines empty (if you write your own footer lines, include the bank details there). With an IBAN, a finalised invoice with a positive total also carries an EPC QR code that banking apps scan to pre-fill the transfer. The IBAN is checked for format and check digits as you type, the BIC for its 8- or 11-character format.
  • Website, company register number, register court and country code — stored, but not printed automatically; add them to the footer lines if they must appear.
  • A logo. Any image from the gallery works: a large photo or graphic is scaled down automatically (to 1200 px, 1 MB) rather than refused, and a message tells you the new size; an image already within those limits is stored unchanged, and a file the device cannot read as an image is refused. Each image row has Upload and, once set, Remove; the form shows a short code for the stored image, not a preview — use a document preview to see the result.
  • Logo size on documents — Small, Medium or Large. On quotes, delivery notes and invoices the logo is fitted into a 55 × 13, 85 × 20 or 115 × 28 mm box. The same choice enlarges the logo on certificates: about 12, 18 or 25 mm high, and at most 85 mm (Medium) or 110 mm (Large) wide. The logo is never cropped or stretched.
  • A banner image — letterhead-style artwork printed across the full width at the top of every page of quotes, delivery notes, invoices and inspection certificates (up to 30 mm tall, fitted). Upload it separately from the logo (scaled to 2400 px, 1 MB). The image keeps its proportions, so artwork that is not as wide as the page leaves room beside it — choose its position (left, centred or right) with the three alignment buttons that appear under the banner image once one is set. On quotes, delivery notes and invoices a banner image can stand alone. On certificates the title row always carries a logo: without your own, the built-in HDX logo prints under the banner — upload a logo if you do not want it.
  • A banner tagline (the slogan) — text printed in a coloured strip under the header of quotes, delivery notes and invoices; leave it empty for no strip. The banner colour is a hex code such as #0E5BD8; left empty, the strip uses the certificate accent colour. Once a tagline is typed, three buttons set its alignment (left unless you change it).
  • The certificate accent colour — one of eight preset colours for the certificate's rule and headings.
  • Footer lines — one per line, as many as you need (three or four fit comfortably), with an alignment (centred unless you change it) for documents. With no footer lines, documents print an automatic footer: name and address, phone and e-mail, bank, IBAN, BIC and UID. On certificates the footer lines replace the standard closing note under the declarations and stay left-aligned; leave them empty to keep the standard note. Documents and certificates already issued keep the alignment and position they were issued with.
  • Small business scheme (§ 6 Abs. 1 Z 27 UStG) — switch it on before issuing small-business-exempt invoices; without it such an invoice is refused. Whether the scheme applies to you is for your tax adviser.
  • Signatory name and title and an optional stored issuer signature, printed on quotes only. Delivery notes, invoices and cancellation invoices carry no issuer block.
  • Default payment term and default document language for new documents.
  • Number floors per document type and year — the first number to issue when you move from another system mid-year (e.g. continue at 2026 0231). They are available once the profile has been saved, and each is stored at once with Save floor (a four-digit year and a first number of at least 1). A floor cannot be removed, only overwritten, and one below the highest number already issued has no effect.
  • Default articles for work, travel and distance, attached to the lines the app adds to a delivery note when an inspection is finalised (chapter 11) — and so to the invoice combined from those notes.
  • Text templates — default opening and closing wording per document type and language. The fields start empty, which means the built-in wording is used; type your own to replace it. Delivery notes have no built-in text.

When a check is started on a store with more than one profile, the start sheet asks which profile it is for; the profile is frozen onto the check at finalisation, and documents likewise snapshot the issuer at finalisation (§12.4). Profiles are never deleted. A profile can be archived only while no document, article or inspection refers to it and it is not the default; the app says which applies. An archived profile cannot issue documents and cannot be restored in the app, so archive only a profile created by mistake. Two devices setting different defaults while offline produce a default conflict banner that is resolved by confirming one.

13.3a Certificate settings (Admin)#

Certificate settings (Zertifikatseinstellungen, formerly “certificate branding”) keeps the process settings for PDF certificates; the company identity, logo and colour now live on the company profile above. An administrator (or an inspector granted Organisation settings) opens it from Settings; other inspectors can view it but not change it. From here you can set:

  • The default language for new customers (Deutsch or English), which is also the working language for checklist templates (§10.1).
  • How many photos per item appear on the certificate (1–20; extra photos stay on record and are noted).
  • Whether to include the photo section and the per-item notes on certificates at all.
  • Optional inspector and customer declaration wording.

The certificate footer is no longer set here: it is the company profile's footer lines (§13.3).

Branding is snapshotted per certificate

Branding is captured onto each check when it is finalised, so changing branding here only affects future certificates — certificates already issued keep the branding they were issued with. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

Override text is bilingual or not at all

If you override a declaration, you must supply it in both English and German (or neither); each may be up to 1000 characters. This keeps a German certificate from falling back to English wording. The editor shows the error under the field as you type and will not save until it is fixed.

13.3b Articles (Admin / Billing)#

Articles (Artikel) is the catalogue of services and materials you put on documents. Each article has an article number (the next free one is suggested), a German name and description (English optional — the German is printed when no English exists), a unit (hour, litre, kilogram, flat rate, piece, metre, kilometre, day or month), a category, the net sale price with a gross preview, an optional purchase price, the VAT rate (20 %, 13 %, 10 %, 0 %), a service / material flag, optionally the one company profile it is restricted to, and optionally a linked machine that is pre-selected on the line. Search and category chips filter the list. Articles are never deleted: archive one you no longer use (Archive in the title bar); it stays on existing documents and can be restored. If two devices gave the same article number to different articles while apart, a red notice names the numbers after sync; renumber one.

13.4 Connecting Google and setting the Drive store (Admin)#

In Connected mode, an administrator links Google and points the app at the shared folder:

  1. Under Google account (Drive access), tap Connect and complete the Google sign-in. (This grants Drive access only; it is not your app login.)
  2. Under Drive store, either tap Set up Drive store automatically to create or find an “HDX Inspect Data Store” folder in your Drive, or tap the Drive store row (pencil icon) to paste a Drive folder id. The store is validated when you save it.

If your Drive holds several folders named “HDX Inspect Data Store”, automatic set-up stops and asks you to remove or rename the duplicates, or to set the store by its folder id.

Once Google is connected, the account tile shows an overflow (⋮) menu with two more actions:

  • Switch account — clears the connection on this device and re-opens the Google account chooser so you can connect a different Google account. The configured Drive store is left in place.
  • Disconnect — revokes Google Drive access on this device and clears the connected account (after a confirmation). Your Drive files are not deleted; the device simply stops syncing until an account is connected again.

Adding a device, not starting over

When you are bringing an additional device online, connect the same Google account and point it at the same store the office already uses — automatic set-up will find the existing folder, or paste the existing folder ID. Pointing a new device at a different account or folder gives it a separate, empty dataset. The full step-by-step is in §2.2.

Switching stores is confirmed, never silent

Set up Drive store automatically is a set-up action, not a repair. If this device already has a Drive store, it first looks for the standard folder. If it finds a different one — or none, so a new, empty one would have to be created — the app stops and asks you to confirm the switch before anything is created or saved, naming the folder IDs. Switching publishes this device's data into the other folder and ends syncing with the current store and the devices that use it — only confirm if you deliberately want a new, separate shared store. Choosing Cancel changes nothing, in Drive or on the device. If sync is failing, use Re-check Drive store (shown once a store is set): it verifies the configured folder is reachable, reconnects the Drive client and syncs again without ever changing the folder; or read the error under Details (§17).

If Google returns a configuration error, a diagnostic banner explains it (for example, the Drive API not being enabled, or a misconfigured OAuth client) and shows the address of the right page in the Google Cloud Console as text you can copy — including this build's package name and signing fingerprint where relevant.

13.5 Sync status and conflicts#

The Synchronisation row shows when the device last synced and how many operations are pending; anyone can tap Sync now to push and pull immediately. If the last sync failed, a Details button opens the full error text, and a banner under the app header also reports a sync error or conflicts that need a decision until you dismiss it; tapping the sync badge in the header opens the same place. If two devices changed the same record while apart, the change lands in Sync conflicts, which any signed-in user can open. Each conflict shows the record, when it was detected and, field by field, the value on This device, the Incoming value and what it Was; a deletion that met an edit is flagged in red. Choose Keep this device or Keep incoming and confirm: the chosen version replaces the other on every device at the next sync, and this cannot be undone. Concurrent edits to different records merge automatically; same-record edits wait here for a human, so a change is never silently overwritten.

13.6 Accounts & devices (Admin)#

Accounts & devices is the admin registry of app logins and trusted devices. (Everyone also has a Change my password tile in Settings for their own login — see §2.4.)

  • Accounts — create an account: enter the username, name, optional email, the role (Inspector or Admin — it cannot be changed later) and a temporary password of your choosing that meets the password policy, and pass it to the user yourself; they must replace it at first sign-in. Edit a name (fix a typo in someone's display name — your admin password is required, and the change syncs to every device); reset a password by typing a new temporary one; deactivate / reactivate an account; or delete an account outright. Deactivate keeps the account (it just can't sign in); Delete removes it permanently and syncs that removal to every device. Either way, the person's past inspection records and certificates are kept — deletion removes the login, not the work. You cannot deactivate or delete the last active admin, nor deactivate your own account (the app blocks it), and you delete your own account from Settings, not here (§2.4). Each row is tagged active / inactive, and shows when the user must still change their password and how many permissions they hold.
  • Permissions — grant an inspector individual admin capabilities (see §13.6a below).
  • Devices — each install registers itself when a user signs in, and appears with a platform name (for example Android tablet, iPhone, Windows PC) and a device code (used in certificate numbers). The device you are currently using is listed first and badged This device. Each row shows when that device was last seen. An admin can mark a device untrusted and trust it again; today this is a label in this list only.

Why another device may take a few minutes to appear

A newly signed-in device publishes itself on its next sync, and other devices pick it up on their next sync — so a device (or a newly created account) can take a short while to show up everywhere. The name is the platform only, never your hardware model, so two devices of the same kind share a label and are told apart by the code and the This device badge.

Best practice — create each account once

Give every person a single account here and have them use it on all of their devices (including offline). Don't create a separate account per device for the same person: accounts are keyed by a hidden id, so a duplicate is a distinct login that doesn't share the original's history. When setting up a new device, let the existing accounts sync down rather than re-creating them (§2.2).

Honest limitation

Marking a device untrusted restricts nothing: it does not block the device, does not appear on the Dashboard and does not flag its data. Deactivating an account stops sign-in on a device once that device has synced the change. A fully offline device cannot be cut off remotely — there is no server and no remote wipe. To cut a device off, remove its Google account's access to the Drive store.

13.6a Per-user permissions (Admin)#

On an inspector's row, the menu has a Permissions entry that opens a set of toggles. Each toggle grants that inspector one area of the admin surface; turning all of them on gives them the same in-app abilities as an administrator, without changing their role. Saving requires your admin password.

PermissionWhat it grants
Bookings & planningCreate, edit and cancel bookings (and the dashboard's New booking button).
Customers & machinesCreate and edit customers, machines and machine types.
TemplatesThe Templates tab: author and edit checklist templates.
Certificates: void & supersedeVoid or supersede finalised certificates (password re-confirmed per action).
BillingQuotes, invoices and cancellation invoices (create, finalise, mark paid, cancel, void), the article catalogue, the customers' billing details and the dashboard's billing tiles. Delivery notes need no grant — every signed-in user can write and sign one.
Accounts & devicesManage user accounts and device trust — including granting these permissions to others.
Organisation settings & device administrationGoogle Drive connection and store, company profiles, certificate settings, data retention and the device wipe.
  • Changes take effect at that user's next sign-in on each device (after the change has synced there).
  • Nobody can change their own permissions — not even an admin (an admin already has everything).
  • The permission toggles only appear on inspector rows; administrators always hold every capability.
  • The app still requires at least one active administrator account: a fully-granted inspector does not count as the last admin for the deactivate/delete safety guards.

Honest limitation

Permissions are an application-layer convenience, exactly like the admin/inspector role itself. Anyone with access to the Google Drive store can read or change all underlying data regardless of these toggles — and an inspector granted Accounts & devices can manage accounts, so treat that grant as equivalent to making them an admin.

13.7 Audit log#

Audit log is a read-only record of significant actions (creates, updates, sign-offs, finalisations, voids, supersedes, exports, distributions and conflict resolutions). It lists the 200 most recent entries, newest first: the kind of record and the action, the time, the acting account's internal id and any detail. Any signed-in user can view it. It is held on the device and included in the synced dataset for a consolidated view.

Honest limitation

The activity log is best-effort integrity, not a tamper-evident trail. The synced log file is itself editable by anyone with Drive access. A hash chain is checked each time the screen opens and a red warning names the first affected entry if it does not verify; that detects accidental corruption and casual tampering, but the log must never be treated as court-grade or tamper-proof.

13.8 Danger zone#

In Connected mode everyone sees a red Danger zone. Delete my account is available to every user (§2.4). The data-retention controls and the device wipe need the Organisation settings permission (administrators have it); for everyone else they are shown locked and explain why when tapped. The destructive actions require re-entering your password.

Retention period

Retention period sets how long finalised records are kept before an admin can purge them. The default is Keep forever — nothing is ever deleted automatically; retention is strictly opt-in. You can choose 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 or 10 years (7 years is marked as the recommended value for Austrian record-keeping) or switch back to keep-forever at any time. Setting the period deletes nothing by itself.

This setting is stored on this device only — it does not sync, so set it on the device an admin will run the purge from. (The purge's deletions, by contrast, do sync to every device.)

Retention purge

Once a retention period is set, Delete records past retention lets an admin purge finalised checks older than the period. The app shows how many records will be removed, asks for your password, then deletes and syncs the change to all devices, which remove the purged checks' photos and PDFs from their own storage at their next sync. Customers, machines and the audit log are not affected, and each purge is recorded in the audit log. If no period is set the action is disabled with a hint; if nothing is old enough, the app says so and deletes nothing.

Wipe this device

Wipe this device deletes the local database on this device, destroys its encryption key and signs this device out of Google. If there is unsynced work, the app lists what would be lost and stops: cancel and sync first, or choose Force wipe to lose it. After a successful wipe a final screen offers Close app; reopen the app to start fresh.

Honest limitation

The wipe removes the database and its key. Photos, signatures and PDFs already saved as files on the device are not removed by it — uninstall the app or clear its storage to remove them.

Important — read this

A device wipe is local-only and cannot be undone. It removes this device's copy and its key; it does not delete anything from the Google Drive store. It signs the device out of Google but does not withdraw the access that Google account has to the Drive store — that is a separate step an administrator performs in Google. Always let unsynced work sync before wiping.

14. Working offline & how sync works#

HDX Inspect is built to work without a signal. Everything you do — inspections, bookings, customer and machine edits — is saved to the device immediately and queued for sync. When the device next reaches Google Drive, the queued changes are published and everyone else's changes are pulled in.

  • Nothing is lost to a flat battery or a dropped connection. Captured work is durable locally before the app confirms it, and stays in the device's queue until it is confirmed merged into the shared store.
  • Multi-writer sync. Any device can publish; the app uses numbered revisions behind a single committed pointer so readers never see a half-written dataset and a lost race is always recoverable.
  • Conflicts are surfaced, not hidden. Same-record edits made on two devices wait in Sync conflicts for a person to choose (§13.5).
  • Store problems fail loud. A missing or unwritable store, a full Drive quota, or expired Google access block sync visibly and prompt you to fix them — sync never silently does nothing.
  • Sync retries itself. A momentary drop, a stale Drive listing (“File not found” for a file that was just removed) or an expired Google token is retried inside the same sync; if a sync still fails, the app re-tries every few minutes while something is owed — a failed sync, unpublished work, or no completed sync yet in this session — and again as soon as the device is back online. A device with nothing to publish does not re-publish on a timer; every few minutes it only checks whether another device has published and, if so, pulls that in — records and the photos, signatures and PDFs they reference. Files another device has not finished uploading yet are fetched on a later check without any further action.

Sync early and often

Two things depend on syncing, so sync early and often:

• If a device is lost or destroyed before it ever syncs, work captured only on it is gone — encryption does not help here. The fix is to keep the offline window short.

• There is currently no limit on how long a device may work offline: checks can be finalised without ever syncing. A 7-day offline window is planned but not active, so keeping the offline period short is a matter of discipline. (Invoices are different: they finalise only right after a successful sync, §12.4.)

• Sync runs only while someone is signed in (§2.6).

Honest limitation

Google Drive revision history is not a backup. A periodic copy of the head revision, binaries and certificates to a second location is an operator responsibility (§16).

16. Important notes & honest limitations#

HDX Inspect is a net improvement on the paper process it replaces, and it is deliberate about what it does not guarantee. Because there is no central server, several protections you might assume are simply not claimed. Please read these.

  • Drive access is the real boundary. In-app roles only shape the UI. Anyone granted access to the Drive store can read or change all underlying data regardless of role. Manage Drive sharing carefully.
  • Records are not tamper-proof. Files in Drive can be edited or deleted by anyone with store access, like a paper record. Finalised checks are write-once by the app's behaviour, not enforced by storage. The audit log is best-effort integrity, not a tamper-evident trail.
  • Distribution is handoff, not delivery. The app records that a report was handed off (and your attestation that you sent it); it cannot confirm a recipient received it.
  • Encryption protects a lost or stolen, locked device. It does not defend against someone using an unlocked, signed-in device, and it has nothing to do with Drive-access exposure. There is no remote wipe.
  • A wipe is local-only. It never deletes Drive-side data; revoking a device's Drive access is a separate operational step. It removes the database and its key, not the photo, signature and PDF files already saved on the device (§13.8).
  • “Untrusted” is only a label. Marking a device untrusted blocks nothing (§13.6), and there is no limit yet on how long a device may work offline (chapter 14).
  • The app sends no e-mail. Certificates and documents leave the device only when a person shares or prints them.
  • Backups are the operator's job. Drive revision history is not a backup; arrange a periodic copy to a second location.
  • Credentials live in the shared file. Accounts are hashed with a strong algorithm, but anyone with Drive access can copy the file and attempt offline cracking — which is why strong passwords are required.
  • Invoices: the app checks, it does not certify. It blocks finalising an invoice whose § 11 UStG mandatory contents are missing, but it does not verify UIDs against VIES, does not choose the VAT treatment (you do — reverse charge, intra-Community supply and exemptions are your call), is not a cash register under the RKSV (cash receipts are not signed or chained — see §12.5), produces no structured e-invoice, and keeps documents write-once by the app's behaviour only. Retention under § 132 BAO and your accounting process remain the operator's responsibility.
  • Document numbers are detected, not reserved. Two devices that finalise invoices while apart can issue the same number; the app spots this after sync, blocks sharing the affected documents and shows a banner — it never renumbers silently (§12.7).

Honest limitation

If a stronger guarantee — tamper-evidence, or access control that a user cannot bypass — is ever required (for example by an inspection regulation), it needs a small server-backed component. The current design is appropriate where that is not required, and is honest about the difference.

17. Troubleshooting & FAQ#

The Share / print button on an invoice is disabled.

  • A finalised invoice or cancellation invoice can be shared only after its record has reached the Drive store (so every device sees the number). Wait for the sync indicator, or tap Sync now beside the button; in Demo mode this is immediate.
  • A document whose number collides with one issued on another device cannot be shared until the collision is resolved (§12.7).
  • A voided document is not shared, and the button waits while the PDF is still pending.
  • Drafts can always be shared — as previews marked Entwurf / Draft, with no number.

Two invoices have the same number.

Two devices finalised while offline. The app does not renumber: decide which document stands, void the other and re-issue it; the next finalisation continues after the highest number in use. Only a void lifts the block in the current version (§12.7).

My new quote (or invoice) disappeared.

A new document is stored only once it has a customer. If you left the editor before choosing one, nothing was kept. Choose the customer first, then enter the lines (§12.3).

Where are my bank details on the invoice?

They print in the page footer when the company profile's footer lines are empty. If you wrote your own footer lines, add the bank details to them (§13.3). The EPC QR code appears on finalised invoices with a positive total when the profile has an IBAN.

There is an HDX logo on my certificate.

A certificate's title row always carries a logo. If the company profile has none — even when it has a banner image — the built-in HDX logo is printed. Upload your own logo on the profile (§13.3).

I have the Billing permission but cannot edit the company profile.

Company profiles are edited with the Organisation settings permission, not Billing. Ask an administrator to grant it, or to make the change (§13.3, §13.6a).

I can't sign in.

  • Check the username and password. After five wrong passwords in a row the account is locked on that device for 15 minutes.
  • If you were given a temporary password, the first sign-in forces you to set a new one.
  • If your account was deactivated, an administrator must reactivate it (Settings → Accounts & devices).

I forgot my password.

Ask an administrator to reset it in Settings → Accounts & devices → Reset password on their device. They will give you a temporary password to change at your next sign-in. There is no self-service reset — there is no server to send a reset email. If the reset was made on another device, tap Trouble signing in? → Check for account updates on the sign-in screen so the reset reaches your device (§2.3).

How do I delete my account?

Open Settings → Danger zone → Delete my account, read what it explains, and confirm with your password. Your login is removed from every device and you are signed out; the inspection records and certificates you created stay with the organisation. It cannot be undone. If you are the last active administrator, a second administrator account must be created first (an inspector cannot be promoted). An administrator can also delete another person's account from Settings → Accounts & devices (§13.6).

How do I set up a second device, or use the same account on more than one device?

  • You don't copy or recreate accounts. On the new device choose Join an existing store, connect the same Google account and Drive folder, let the existing accounts and data sync down, then sign in with your normal account. The full procedure is in §2.2.
  • One account can be used on as many devices as you like, including offline — each device just needs to sync with the shared store. Re-creating an account with the same username on another device makes a different account, not the same one.

The sync badge is red / sync isn't working.

  • On Settings → Synchronisation, tap Details (shown when there is an error) to read it. It starts with the step that failed (pull, download binaries, file certificates, push …) followed by what Drive answered.
  • A brief network hiccup is retried automatically (a few times, with a short pause) before the badge turns red, so a momentary drop usually clears itself — and it keeps retrying every few minutes after that, and as soon as the device is back online.
  • Common causes of a persistent red badge: no internet (it retries when back online); the Drive store is unreachable or not writable; the Drive quota is full; Google access expired and must be reconnected by an admin; or nobody is signed in — sync runs only while someone is.
  • To reconnect a device whose store is fine, use Settings → Drive store → Re-check Drive store: it verifies the configured folder, reconnects the Drive client and syncs again without changing anything.
  • Do not use Set up Drive store automatically to clear a sync error on a device that already has a store. It is a set-up action: if it finds a different folder, or none, it would move this device to a separate store (the app now asks before doing so — see the next question).
  • Your work is safe locally and will sync once the problem is resolved.

Sync says “File not found: …” — but the Drive store is still there.

  • Google Drive's folder listings lag a little behind deletions: a file that another device (or this one, on its previous sync) just removed can still be listed for a moment, and reading it then answers “File not found”. The same wording appears when a folder the app remembered has been trashed or recreated under it.
  • The app now treats this as temporary: it forgets the folder locations it had cached, re-reads the store and re-runs the sync by itself — in the same attempt and, if needed, on the next automatic retry. You should not need to do anything. If it persists, Re-check Drive store (§13.4) reconnects without changing the folder.
  • If the error names your Drive store folder itself (the ID shown under Settings → Drive store), the message says so and explains the remedy: restore the folder from the Drive trash, or reconnect the Google account that owns it. Only Set up Drive store automatically if you really want to start a new, empty shared store — it does not reconnect the device to the existing data, and the app asks you to confirm before switching.

A certificate says “Certificate pending”.

The check finalised but the PDF could not be generated. Tap Retry certificate on the completion screen. If you have left it, open the Dashboard: it retries automatically and shows a red card with Retry now. Opening the check from Reports meanwhile shows only a regenerated preview. The record itself is never lost because the PDF failed.

I can't finalise an invoice — it says I must sync.

An invoice or cancellation invoice can only be finalised right after a successful sync, so its number is based on the latest data. Connect, sync (Settings → Sync now), then finalise. Checks, quotes and delivery notes finalise offline (§12.4).

There are sync conflicts.

Two devices changed the same record while apart. Open Settings → Sync conflicts (any user can), compare the values on this device and the incoming ones, and choose Keep this device or Keep incoming. Nothing is overwritten until you decide (§13.5).

Where do I find help or the introduction again?

Tap the ? at the top of any main screen to open this manual at the matching chapter, or open Settings → Help & about for the whole manual and Show the introduction again (§2.7).

I see a red “DB UNENCRYPTED · DEV” banner.

That is a development-only build with encryption deliberately switched off for testing on an emulator. It must never be used for real data — use a normal (encrypted) build.

How do I change the app's language?

Open Settings → Appearance & language and use the Language toggle. It changes the app's interface immediately, on this device only (for everyone who signs in on it). It does not change what language certificates print in — that follows the customer and can be set per check (see the next question).

A certificate came out in the wrong language.

  • A certificate prints in the customer's certificate language, not the app's interface language. Set the customer's language in their record (Customers → edit, §8.1).
  • For an individual check you can switch the language on the Summary screen using the Certificate language control, any time before you sign (§4.4). After finalisation it is fixed — a wrong-language certificate is corrected by voiding or reissuing it (§5.4–5.5).

It won't let me finalise a German certificate.

A German certificate needs German text for every checklist item. If the template hasn't been translated, the app blocks finalisation rather than issuing a half-German certificate. Either switch the certificate language to English on the Summary screen, or ask an administrator to add the German template text (§10).

How do I draw on or mark up a photo?

In a draft check, tap a photo thumbnail on the checklist item to open the annotation editor. Add freehand marks, arrows, rectangles, ellipses or text tags in your choice of colour, then Save (§4.2). Annotations don't alter the original photo and are baked onto a copy when the check is finalised. You can only annotate before signing.

How do I switch to dark mode?

Open Settings → Appearance and choose System, Light or Dark (§13.2). It applies to this device only and has no effect on certificates or exports.

How do I change our logo or the look of the certificate?

The company name, logo, logo size, banner image, accent colour and footer are on Settings → Company profiles (§13.3). The declaration wording, photos per item and which sections appear are on Settings → Certificate settings (§13.3a). Changes apply to future certificates; ones already issued keep their original branding.

My logo is refused as too big — or it prints too small on invoices.

It is no longer refused: any image from the gallery is scaled down automatically when you upload it as the logo or banner image of a company profile (§13.3); only a file the device cannot read as an image is rejected. If the logo prints too small, pick a larger logo size on the profile, or upload it as a banner image to print it across the full width at the top of quotes, delivery notes, invoices and certificates. Documents and certificates already issued keep the header they were issued with.

The slogan banner (or the banner image / footer) sits on the left — can it be centred?

Yes. On the company profile (§13.3) each of the slogan, the footer lines and the banner image has three alignment buttons (left / centred / right) under its field — the slogan's appear once a slogan is entered, the banner image's once an image is uploaded. Tap centred and save; every quote, delivery note, invoice (and, for the banner image, certificate) issued from then on prints it there. Already issued documents and certificates are unchanged. The footer alignment applies to documents only: on certificates the footer text stays left-aligned. The banner image keeps its proportions, which is why artwork that is not as wide as the page leaves room beside it.

How do I connect a different Google account?

In Settings, open the connected Google account's overflow (⋮) menu and choose Switch account to pick another account, or Disconnect to clear the connection entirely (§13.4). Neither deletes anything from Drive.

18. Glossary#

TermMeaning
AnnotationNon-destructive markup drawn on a photo (arrows, shapes, text). The original photo is untouched; the marks are flattened onto a copy when the check is finalised.
AppearanceThe per-device light / dark / system theme (Settings). It never affects certificates or exports.
BookingOne planned customer visit, linking a customer, machines, an inspector and a time. Each machine on it yields its own check.
CheckA single machine's inspection — its checklist answers, readings, work/travel, signatures and result.
CertificateThe numbered PDF produced when a check is finalised, filed to Drive.
Certificate brandingThe look of a certificate: company name, logo and its size, banner image and position, accent colour and footer from the company profile, plus the declaration wording and section options from Certificate settings. Snapshotted onto each certificate at finalisation.
Certificate languageThe language a certificate is printed in — German or English. Follows the customer and is adjustable per check until finalisation; separate from the app's interface language.
FinalisedA check that has been signed off and locked. Write-once at the application layer; corrected only by void or supersede.
TemplateThe checklist for a machine type (or one assigned to an individual machine). Its items are copied onto each check when the check is started.
Blocking / MinorDefect severities on a failed item. Blocking ⇒ overall Fail and reinspection; Minor ⇒ Pass with defects.
OutboxThe on-device queue of changes waiting to sync. Your safety net until a change is confirmed shared.
ConflictTwo devices changed the same record while apart; resolved by a person in Sync conflicts.
Demo / Connected modeDemo is local-only with sync off; Connected enables Google Drive sync.
Drive storeThe configured Google Drive folder that is the shared system of record.
Void / SupersedeCorrections after finalisation — mark a certificate void, or replace it with a linked reissue. Both retain the original. For documents, Void withdraws a numbered document that was not sent; a sent invoice is undone by a cancellation invoice.
Draft (Entwurf)A document without a number that can still be edited or discarded; also an inspection that has been started but not finalised.
Banner image / taglineLetterhead artwork across the top of documents and certificates, and the slogan strip under the header of documents (§13.3).
Number floorThe first number to issue for a document type and year, used when moving from another system mid-year (§13.3).
Introduction / hintsThe welcome tour shown at first sign-in and the one-time hint on each main screen, remembered per person and device (§2.7).
Document (Beleg)A quote (Angebot), delivery note (Lieferschein), invoice (Rechnung) or cancellation invoice (Stornorechnung). Numbered per company profile and type as YYYYNNNN at finalisation; write-once at the application layer afterwards (chapter 12).
Company profileThe issuing company a certificate or document is made out under — identity, UID, bank details, logo, banner image, slogan, colours, footer, signatory, defaults (§13.3). Snapshotted onto each document and certificate at finalisation.
Cancellation invoiceThe only way to undo an invoice that has been shared: a new numbered document with the negative amounts, linked to the original, which becomes Storniert.
Reverse chargeA VAT treatment you choose on a document; the app then forces 0 % lines, requires the customer's UID and prints the statutory note. It does not decide the treatment for you.
Number collisionThe same document number issued on two devices while apart — detected after sync, blocks sharing, never auto-renumbered (§12.7).
PDF pendingA finalised document (or certificate) whose PDF did not render yet; the record is complete, and the Dashboard (and, for documents, the Billing tab) retries the PDF.
